 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 26.04.2018 passed by the learned III Additional Judge and MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru in MVC No.7516/2016.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The appellant/claimant, who sustained injuries in a road traffic accident on 28.06.2016, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 to award just and proper compensation.
The Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.1,12,140/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a.
Being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimant is before this Court.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent - Insurance Company.
4. The accident is of the year 2016, and the claimant was aged about 42 years as on the date of the accident.

In the absence of proof of income, the notional income is assessed at Rs.9,500/- p.m. as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka legal services authority as against Rs.7,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
The claimant admittedly sustained Chip fracture posterior tibial spine left leg (CT Scan).
The doctor who was examined as P.W.2 assessed the permanent physical disability at 13.4%.

to the left lower limb However, the Tribunal without any basis has assessed the permanent physical disability at 4% instead of 6% having regard to the nature of the injuries, and also the avocation of the claimant.

sentences.text:
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant and assessing the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,500/- as against Rs.7000/- assessed by the Tribunal, the appellant is entitled for the enhanced compensation under the following heads:
 Awarded by this Awarded by the  Court Tribunal  Rs. Rs.

Medical Expenses 6,100/- 6,100/-
Loss of income during  28,500/- 14,000/-
laid up period Pain and suffering 40,000/- 30,000/-
Loss of future earning 95,760/- 47,040/-
capacity (9,500x6%x12x14) (7,000x4%x12 x 14)
Nourishment,Conveyance 10,000/- 10,000/-
& attendant charges Loss of amenities 15,000/- 5,000/-
Total 1,95,360/- 1,12,140/-
 NC: 2024:KHC:21841 7.
In all, the appellant/claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.1,95,360/- as against Rs.1,12,140/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation is Rs.83,220/-.
8. To this extent, the award passed by the Tribunal stands modified.
9. The enhanced compensation of Rs.83,220/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of actual realization.
10. The enhanced compensation with interest to be deposited by the respondent - Insurance Company within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
11. The entire enhanced compensation amount with interest to be released in favour of the appellant/claimant.
